patient_information: A 62-year-old male Thai police sergeant major from Kalasin Province in northeast Thailand.
chief_complaint: A solitary mass was incidentally found in the liver during his annual physical check-up.
history_of_present_illness: He denies any clinical symptoms, weight loss, jaundice, or other gastrointestinal symptoms and was referred for further investigations and treatment.
exposure_and_epidemiology: He is from Kalasin Province, northeast Thailand, a region where eating raw or undercooked freshwater fish, frequently containing metacercariae of the liver fluke Opisthorchis viverrini, is common; he later revealed a history of liver fluke infection and praziquantel treatment in the past 10 years.
physical_exam: He appears in good health, shows no jaundice, liver and spleen are not palpable, no liver stigmata are found, and no lymphadenopathy is detected.
labs_and_diagnostics: Liver function tests are normal; HBsAg negative, Anti-HBs 24.13 IU/L, HBeAg negative, Anti-HBc positive, Anti-HCV negative, AFP 2.8 U/mL, CEA 18.96 µg/L, and CA19-9 342.80 U/mL. Abdominal MRI revealed a single solid liver mass in the right liver lobe (segments VI/VII).
differential_diagnosis: Hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), a metastatic tumour, and some infections, including tuberculosis.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient underwent hemihepatectomy for a large (9 × 9 cm) whitish-yellowish tumour in the right liver lobe, where liver flukes were also detected in the adjacent bile duct; he was then started on postoperative chemotherapy.
final_diagnosis: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) with associated Opisthorchis viverrini infection.

The liver parenchyma appears non-cirrhotic; (B) The adjacent dilated bile duct contains a few liver flukes (O. viverrini); and (C) The histology of the tumour shows infiltrative compact glandular structures, lined by dysplastic columnar cells with necrosis.
